checks.s: The memo includes proposed compromise contract language for the Teaming Agreement's work-share allocation provision.
The memo includes proposed compromise contract language for the Teaming Agreement's exclusivity/non-compete provision.
The memo includes proposed compromise contract language for the Teaming Agreement's intellectual property rights in proposal materials provision.
The memo includes proposed compromise contract language for the Teaming Agreement's termination-for-convenience provision.
The proposed work-share compromise sets a minimum percentage for Phalanx of approximately 22–33%, around the 25–30% cost-model range.
The proposed IP clause explicitly states that each party retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property developed or owned prior to or independent of the teaming effort.
The proposed IP clause or its accompanying rationale names PhalanxShield™ as Phalanx's pre-existing intellectual property and states that it is preserved or protected.
The deliverable references U.S. Copyright Registration No. TX-9-384-221 in connection with PhalanxShield™.
The proposed IP clause or its accompanying rationale names CascadeConnect™ as Cascade's pre-existing intellectual property and states that it is preserved or protected.
The exclusivity/non-compete clause or its rationale acknowledges that DLA may award up to three IDIQ contracts under solicitation SP4701-25-R-0040.

The exclusivity/non-compete compromise uses the up-to-three-contract multi-award IDIQ structure under the same solicitation to define, limit, or shape the scope or duration of post-award restrictions.
The termination-for-convenience clause sets different termination terms for before proposal submission and after proposal submission.
The termination-for-convenience clause imposes more restrictive termination conditions after proposal submission than before it.
The termination-for-convenience compromise requires the terminating party to reimburse the non-terminating party for documented bid and proposal (B&P) costs upon termination.
The termination clause sets a maximum B&P cost reimbursement cap greater than $0 and less than $2,500,000.
The memo flags that Greystone Capital Partners, Phalanx's majority private equity investor, holds approval rights over teaming agreements exceeding $50,000,000 in anticipated subcontract value.

The memo states or shows that Phalanx's anticipated subcontract value exceeds the $50,000,000 Greystone board approval threshold at every contemplated work-share percentage, including $72,000,000 at the lowest proposed share of 15% of the $480,000,000 contract ceiling.

The work-share compromise provides a task-order allocation mechanism between Cascade's 'sole discretion' and Phalanx's 'right of first refusal on all cybersecurity-scoped task orders,' such as consultation, preferential consideration, a defined cybersecurity scope carve-out, or a notice-and-opportunity process.
The exclusivity/non-compete compromise imposes a post-award restriction on competing work, particularly Phalanx's competing DLA cybersecurity engagements.
The post-award non-compete restriction expires sooner than 36 months following contract completion, including by lasting only during active performance or another shorter defined period.
The memo provides a written negotiation rationale for the work-share compromise that justifies the middle-ground position and explains why it should be acceptable to both Cascade and Phalanx.

The memo provides a written negotiation rationale for the exclusivity/non-compete compromise that justifies the middle-ground position and explains why it should be acceptable to both Cascade and Phalanx.
The memo provides a written negotiation rationale for the IP rights compromise that justifies the middle-ground position and explains why it should be acceptable to both Cascade and Phalanx.

The memo provides a written negotiation rationale for the termination-for-convenience compromise that justifies the middle-ground position and explains why it should be acceptable to both Cascade and Phalanx.
The IP compromise clause addresses ownership or usage rights for proposal materials jointly developed by Cascade and Phalanx during the teaming effort.
The IP clause provides a framework for jointly developed proposal materials other than sole ownership by Cascade, such as joint ownership or shared rights.
The IP clause limits at least one party's use of jointly developed proposal materials or requires accounting to the other party.

The IP clause imposes at least one specific, defined limitation on using jointly developed proposal materials, such as a restriction on competing proposals, a consent requirement, confidentiality duties, or limits on disclosure to third parties.
